sections.h2: What sets Gahanna apart for a home seller?
sections.html:
Gahanna is a Columbus suburb with its own school district and its own downtown on the creek. Franklin County holds the city, which shares borders with Columbus on three sides, New Albany to the north, and Mifflin and Jefferson townships.

The name comes from a word for three creeks joining into one, and Big Walnut Creek, with its tributaries Rocky Fork Creek and Sycamore Run, still shapes the map. Gahanna and the neighboring village of Bridgeport merged under the Gahanna name, and the village was recorded as incorporated on August 8, 1881. A few small islands of Jefferson Township sit inside the city limits, so confirm with the Franklin County Auditor which taxing districts apply to your parcel.

Three practical items come up for sellers here: how rental registration affects a landlord's sale, what the county charges to transfer title, and how the creek system bears on a parcel.

sections.h2: How do Gahanna homes compare on the Census numbers?
sections.html:
Gahanna's figures run above the national ones in the same Census tables: a median owned-home value of $350,900 against $332,700 for the United States, household income of $109,061 against $80,734, and a bachelor's degree rate of 51.7 percent against 35.7 percent. Seven in ten households own their home.

sections.h2: What does Gahanna require of a landlord selling a rental?
sections.html:
A rental owner needs to know the city's registration rules, because a buyer who keeps the property as a rental must register it within 30 days of the transfer. Gahanna's Ordinance 0053-2018 requires every residential rental owner to register every two years.

The city's rental registration page and its FAQ set out the details:

  • Registration runs between January 1 and March 15, and approved permits expire December 31 of the second year.
  • The fee table lists a $50 registration fee, plus a $100 permit fee for a single-family home or duplex.
  • Multifamily permit fees are $200 under 10 units, $400 for 10 to 59 units, $600 for 60 to 99 units and $800 for 100 or more.
  • Inspectors check the exterior from the sidewalk or right-of-way against the city codes and the International Property Maintenance Code, and no one has to be home.
  • Owner-occupied single-family homes (occupied more than half the year) may request an exemption case by case.
  • Airbnb-style rentals under 30 consecutive days count as short-term rentals and fall under the same program.

If tenants are in place when you sell, ask Code Enforcement whether any violations are open on the permit, since an unresolved report can slow a buyer's lender.

sections.h2: What does Franklin County charge to transfer a Gahanna deed?
sections.html:
The Franklin County Auditor bills $3 per $1,000 of price on a standard sale, split between a $1 state share and a $2 county share, and adds a $0.50 transfer tax. Use the Auditor's online calculator, which asks you to round the price up to the next $100 and applies a $3 floor.

The county share is waived when the seller holds the homestead exemption on the transfer date, which cuts the rate to $1 per $1,000. An exempt conveyance owes just the $0.50. The calculator page accepts cash, business checks and cashier's checks payable to the Franklin County Auditor and turns away personal checks, and the amount must be exact.

ORC 319.202 puts the statement of value on the buyer's side and makes the seller pay the fee. Value includes any mortgage or lien. The Transfer and Conveyance department answers questions at 614-525-3253.

Homestead status is worth checking before you sign. The Auditor FAQ says the standard credit goes to owners aged 65 by year-end or permanently and totally disabled, within an income cap, while disabled veterans at 100 percent can qualify for an enhanced credit with no income test.

sections.h2: Who are Gahanna's buyers and what draws them?
sections.html:
Gahanna works as a commuter base: Interstate 670 and US 62 lead to John Glenn Columbus International Airport, Interstate 270 rings the area, Ohio 317 is the main north-south street through downtown, and COTA runs bus lines 24 and 25 through the center.

The Gahanna-Jefferson Public School District serves the city. According to Wikipedia, it runs seven elementary schools, three middle schools and Gahanna-Lincoln High School, and private options include Columbus Academy and Gahanna Christian Academy.

Downtown redevelopment has been part of the pitch since 2004. The Creekside project added a public park extension, restaurants, offices, residences and a 389-space garage. The city also runs a brownfields program with a community-wide inventory, assessments, and demolition of abandoned or environmentally suspect buildings. On the former Bedford I Landfill, a 200-acre cleanup became Central Park of Gahanna, home to a golf academy.

sections.h2: How does Gahanna's creek system affect a house sale?
sections.html:
Properties along Big Walnut Creek, Rocky Fork Creek and Sycamore Run deserve a flood and drainage check before listing, since the creeks have a significant effect on the local geography.

Ask the Franklin County Auditor's office or the city for the zone of your parcel, and keep any insurance, drainage or sump-pump records handy. A documented dry basement and a clear drainage path answer the question before a buyer raises it.

sections.h2: What are the options for selling a Gahanna house fast?
sections.html:
• Agent listing: reaches mortgage-backed buyers, who will expect a clean inspection.
  • Direct sale: no commission, but you handle the disclosure form, DTE 100 and deed paperwork.
  • Investor purchase: useful when the home needs updating, a tenant is in place or you must close on a set date.

Ohio sellers of one-to-four unit homes complete the state disclosure form. Compare offers on the amount you take home after the conveyance fee, the tax proration and any loan payoff.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Gahanna rental that is registered with the city?
faqs.a: Yes, registration does not stop a sale. A buyer who keeps it as a rental registers within 30 days after the transfer, and any open violation is best cleared first.

faqs.q: How much is the Franklin County conveyance fee on a Gahanna sale?
faqs.a: Standard sales run $3 per $1,000 plus the $0.50 transfer tax, and sellers with homestead at transfer pay $1 per $1,000. Run your price through the Auditor's calculator for the exact figure.

faqs.q: Where do I ask about homestead before a Gahanna closing?
faqs.a: The Franklin County Auditor's Homestead office handles it, at 373 S High St, 21st Floor, Columbus, or homestead@franklincountyohio.gov. Whether you hold it on the closing date decides the conveyance rate.

faqs.q: Which school district covers Gahanna houses?
faqs.a: Gahanna-Jefferson Public Schools, whose high school is Gahanna-Lincoln. Small Jefferson Township pockets sit within city limits, so verify the district for your address with the county.

faqs.q: Who pays the conveyance fee when a Gahanna house sells?
faqs.a: The seller pays under ORC 319.202, and the buyer files the statement of value. Your purchase contract may restate or shift it, so read the closing section.
